knowledgeBases.title: Cricket rules desk
knowledgeBases.description: Original summaries of the MCC Laws of Cricket and ICC international playing conditions. Claims record when each rule took effect and whether it applies to club cricket under the Laws or to international matches, which sometimes changed on different dates.

showcase.title: New edition of the Laws
showcase.question: Is a bunny-hop boundary catch allowed in club cricket?
showcase.lesson: The 2026 MCC Laws took effect on 1 October 2026: a fielder may touch the ball only once while airborne beyond the rope. The older rule that allowed it applied until 30 September 2026.

showcase.title: Same date, different level
showcase.question: Was a bunny-hop boundary catch allowed in club cricket on 2026-03-01?
showcase.lesson: On 1 March 2026, club cricket still followed the old Law, while international cricket had banned the bunny hop since June 2025. One date, two correct answers, depending on the level.

showcase.title: Depends on the format
showcase.question: How long does a new batter have to be ready?
showcase.lesson: Club cricket under the Laws allows three minutes, Tests and ODIs two, and T20 internationals 90 seconds. TruthGraph asks for the match type instead of guessing.

showcase.title: Rule replaced
showcase.question: After a batter is caught, who faces the next ball?
showcase.lesson: Since October 2022 the new batter always faces, whether or not the batters crossed. Older explanations still describe the crossing rule.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: allowed if the last ground contact before the first touch was inside the boundary
claims.statement: Under the MCC Laws before the 2026 edition, only a fielder's last contact with the ground before first touching the ball had to be inside the boundary, so a fielder could leap from beyond the rope, touch the ball more than once while airborne, and still take a fair catch.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: only one airborne touch allowed from beyond the boundary
claims.statement: Since the 2026 edition of the MCC Laws took effect on 1 October 2026, a fielder who jumps from beyond the boundary may touch the ball only once while airborne; any later contact with the ground outside the boundary during that delivery scores a boundary. This ends bunny-hop catches in cricket played under the Laws.

relations.reason: The 2026 edition of the MCC Laws rewrote Law 19.5.2 to allow only one airborne touch from beyond the boundary.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: allowed, as under the MCC Law
claims.statement: Until ICC changed its playing conditions in June 2025, international cricket followed the MCC Law on boundary catches, which allowed repeated airborne touches beyond the rope if the last ground contact before the first touch was inside the boundary.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: only one airborne touch allowed from beyond the boundary
claims.statement: ICC playing conditions introduced the one-airborne-touch boundary-catch rule before the MCC Laws did: from 17 June 2025 in Tests, 2 July 2025 in ODIs, and 10 July 2025 in T20 internationals.

relations.reason: ICC adopted the new boundary-catch rule in its June 2025 playing conditions, ahead of the MCC Laws.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: using saliva to shine the ball
claims.value: banned
claims.statement: Since 1 October 2022 the MCC Laws and ICC playing conditions both ban saliva on the ball; sweat is the only natural substance allowed, and using saliva is treated like any other unfair change to the ball's condition. The ban made a temporary Covid-era international measure permanent.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: who faces the next ball after a catch
claims.value: depended on whether the batters crossed
claims.statement: Before 1 October 2022, if the batters had crossed before a catch was taken, the not-out batter stayed at the striker's end to face the next ball and the new batter went to the non-striker's end.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: who faces the next ball after a catch
claims.value: the new batter faces the next ball
claims.statement: Since 1 October 2022, when a batter is out caught, the incoming batter goes to the striker's end and faces the next ball whether or not the batters crossed, unless the over has ended.

relations.reason: The 2022 Laws and ICC playing conditions made the new batter face the next ball regardless of crossing.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: time for the incoming batter to be ready
claims.value: 3 minutes
claims.statement: Under MCC Law 40, an incoming batter must be ready to receive the ball, or for the partner to receive it, within three minutes of the dismissal or retirement, or may be given out timed out on appeal.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: time for the incoming batter to be ready
claims.value: 2 minutes
claims.statement: Since 1 October 2022, ICC playing conditions require an incoming batter in a Test to be ready to take strike within two minutes, shorter than the three minutes in the MCC Laws.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: time for the incoming batter to be ready
claims.value: 2 minutes
claims.statement: Since 1 October 2022, ICC playing conditions require an incoming batter in an ODI to be ready to take strike within two minutes, shorter than the three minutes in the MCC Laws.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: time for the incoming batter to be ready
claims.value: 90 seconds
claims.statement: In T20 internationals, ICC playing conditions give an incoming batter ninety seconds to be ready to take strike; the 2022 changes kept this threshold.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: eleven
claims.statement: A cricket match is played between two sides of eleven players, one of whom is captain. Sides may agree to play with fewer or more, but no more than eleven may field at any time.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: out only if every LBW condition applies
claims.statement: A batter is out LBW only if all of these apply: the delivery is not a no ball; the ball pitches in line between wicket and wicket or on the off side, so a ball pitching outside leg stump cannot be LBW; it hits the batter's person without first touching the bat; the impact is in line, or outside off stump when no genuine shot is offered; and the ball would otherwise have hit the wicket.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: junior cricket only
claims.statement: Before the 2026 edition of the MCC Laws, laminated bats were legal only in junior cricket.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: allowed in open-age cricket at lower levels
claims.statement: Since the 2026 edition of the MCC Laws took effect on 1 October 2026, laminated (Type D) bats are legal in open-age cricket, not only junior cricket, at the lower levels of the game set by each country's governing body.

relations.reason: The 2026 edition extended laminated bats from junior cricket to open-age cricket.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: six valid balls
claims.statement: The ball is bowled from each end in turn, in overs of six valid balls; wides and no balls do not count as one of the six.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: bowling two overs in a row
claims.value: not allowed
claims.statement: A bowler may not bowl two overs in a row, or parts of two consecutive overs, in the same innings.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: off the bat and first landing beyond the boundary
claims.statement: A six is scored only if the ball was hit by the bat and first lands beyond the boundary without touching the ground inside the field.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: reaches the boundary after bouncing, or not off the bat
claims.statement: A four is scored when the ball reaches the boundary after first touching the ground inside the field, or when it crosses the boundary without having been hit by the bat.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: only a throw towards the wickets
claims.statement: Since the 2026 edition of the MCC Laws (1 October 2026), runs for an overthrow apply only when a fielder throws the ball towards the wickets; a ball that crosses the boundary after a fielder's attempt to stop it is a misfield, not an overthrow.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: one run plus any runs scored
claims.statement: A no ball gives the batting side one penalty run immediately, in addition to any runs scored from that ball. The bowler's front foot must land with some part of it behind the popping crease, or it is a no ball.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: one run
claims.statement: A wide gives the batting side one penalty run immediately, in addition to any other runs, and the ball does not count as one of the over.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: a fair catch off the bat before the ball touches the ground
claims.statement: A batter is out caught when a fair delivery, not a no ball, touches the bat and is then held by a fielder before it touches the ground.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: 200 runs in a 5-day match
claims.statement: In a two-innings match, the side batting first can make the other side follow on if it leads by at least 200 runs in a match of five days or more, 150 in a three- or four-day match, 100 in a two-day match, or 75 in a one-day match.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.value: retired not out if hurt; retired out otherwise unless allowed back
claims.statement: A batter who retires through illness, injury, or another unavoidable cause may resume and is otherwise recorded as retired not out. A batter who retires for any other reason may return only with the opposing captain's consent, and is otherwise recorded as retired out.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: ball hitting a fielder's helmet on the ground
claims.value: 5 penalty runs and dead ball
claims.statement: If the ball in play hits a fielding side's helmet lying on the ground, the ball becomes dead and the batting side is awarded 5 penalty runs.

claims.subject: Cricket
claims.predicate: wicket in the last over of the day
claims.value: the over is completed
claims.statement: Since the 2026 edition of the MCC Laws (1 October 2026), if a wicket falls in the final over of a day in multi-day cricket after the time for close of play, the over is bowled in full instead of stumps being drawn.
